title: Rudolf Blaschka 1892 — yield ontology and quantitative statement register
purpose: Operationalize pass26 by recording major 1892 quantities according to what each source actually counts. The register deliberately preserves incompatible totals where they belong to different dates, actors, media or operations.

rows.statement: The parties decide not to bind themselves to 60 species.
rows.do_not_read_as: expedition collection target or actual model output

rows.statement: Fifty will be the minimum while the makers will produce as many as can comfortably be made.
rows.do_not_read_as: number Rudolf must collect during travel

rows.statement: Rudolf sends about 29 species of Cambridge Botanic Garden seeds to Hosterwitz as a sample without value, with sowing instructions.

rows.source: BLA-D00725 / 017:79 (Hope Garden letter; record page visible in compact/full OCR)
rows.statement: Before leaving Jamaica Rudolf says he has finished his work with 106 species.
rows.do_not_read_as: necessarily 106 colour drawings, 106 herbarium sheets, or 106 later models

rows.source: Foreign Students in the Gardens, Bulletin of the Botanical Department, Jamaica, p.18
rows.unit: species represented by accurate coloured drawings
rows.statement: The Jamaican institutional report states that Blaschka made accurate coloured drawings of 116 species; Cameron made dried collections of the same and other plants.
rows.do_not_read_as: a correction of Rudolf's 106 without reconciling date/category/reporting practice

rows.statement: After substantial drawing Rudolf says he now has ten interesting species.
After ignoring most very small plants and selecting showy/characteristic forms, Rudolf says the useful species total is 25.
rows.do_not_read_as: all species encountered or all herbarium specimens

rows.statement: Rudolf says he draws during the day and has finished 25 species in San Diego so far.
At departure Rudolf calls the San Diego stay botanically favorable and says he completed 36 species there, aided especially by Orcutt's procurement of plant material.
Rudolf reports that he has drawn and studied 200 species up to that point.
rows.do_not_read_as: preserved specimens, later model count, or unique nonduplicate Harvard additions

rows.statement: Rudolf thinks he may have collected/assembled 400 by the time he leaves America.
Rudolf says reaching 600–800 species would require spending the whole year wandering around America.
Rudolf evaluates the material generated through drawing/study as roughly three years of future work.
rows.do_not_read_as: measured production time or contract duration

rows.statement: Goodale writes that in his view Rudolf has material on hand for about four years' work.

key_discrepancy_cases.rule: Preserve both. Rudolf's 106 is 'finished my work with 106 species'; the institutional 116 is 'accurate coloured drawings of 116 species'. Determine whether additional drawings, counting conventions, report compilation, or source transcription account for the ten-unit difference.
The 25 is an interim 'so far' count; 36 is the 4 May departure count. Do not treat as contradiction.
Rudolf and Goodale are independently forecasting future work. Preserve actor and decision context rather than averaging.

strongest_methodological_result: The archive's numbers become more informative when they fail to match. A quantity is evidence only after its operation is specified. Counts move through a chain from target -> working set -> selected set -> completed local set -> cumulative study count -> forecast yield -> institutional drawing report -> future work horizon. Apparent discrepancies can therefore reveal conversion stages rather than errors.
next_steps: Image-check the Jamaica 106 letter and retrieve the original Jamaican bulletin page image side-by-side.
Locate the exact date/source for the San Diego 25 interim count and freeze it in the register.
Add daily/local counts from Jamaica, Arizona, Colorado and St Louis only when their ontology is explicit.
Add packet quantities (29 seed species, two Ganong boxes, cactus/bulb box) in a separate material-packet table instead of merging with species-study totals.
Add actual later model descendants only in a downstream conversion table, preserving lag and selective reactivation.
